findings.title: Repentance before threatened contact
findings.claim: The focus places repentance and protective covering in the interval opened by the preceding warning: cessation comes before the threatened painful contact, so the invitation can be heard as an available interception before that consequence lands.
findings.mechanism: The focus's return and request for covering meet the supplied 5:73 occurrences attributed as the cessation condition and the arrival of harm by contact. Their ordered contact turns the focus from a general statement about forgiveness into a possible interval between restraint and consequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The invitation becomes an actionable opening before harm makes contact, while the plain call to repent and seek forgiveness remains fully recoverable.
findings.containment: This is a qualified contextual reading from a legacy-unbound HFT trace. It preserves the warning in 5:73 and the mercy of 5:74; the packet also leaves open a reading in which the adjacent ayat state consequence and mercy without forming a material shield sequence.

epistemic.reason: The trace has complete supplied anchor coverage and a distinct before/after reading, but its reader identity is legacy_unbound and the two contextual branches have no independent registry descriptors.

findings.title: Return as redirected allegiance and dependence
findings.claim: Turning to Allah in the focus is a reorientation of allegiance and dependence: worship and the plea for protective covering are directed to the one presented as able to hear, know, and act.
findings.mechanism: The named focus destination carries the supplied worshipped-entity facet; 5:72 supplies worship directed to Allah, while 5:76 tests objects lacking power and contrasts Allah as hearing and knowing. The focus's directional return and suffixed request make that contextual contrast address-specific.
findings.reader_payoff: Repentance becomes more than a generic change of attitude: the reader can see allegiance and need being redirected toward the addressee who can receive and answer them.
findings.containment: This contextual reading adds specificity to the focus's call to repent and seek forgiveness. It does not remove the live possibility that the focus primarily calls for ethical retraction without making worship-address the governing relation.

epistemic.reason: The trace has complete supplied anchor coverage and a distinct address-and-dependence change, but its reader identity is legacy_unbound and four contextual branches have no independent registry descriptors.

findings.title: Mercy as re-housing
findings.claim: The paired closing names can be heard as protective mercy that re-houses the returned person: the focus's covering and mercy meet context images of refuge, entry, and a life-bearing enclosure.
findings.mechanism: The focus places protective covering beside mercy, and the supplied HFT trace links that pair to the refuge in 5:72, the entry in 5:84, and the garden in 5:85. Their contact changes mercy from an appended quality into an exploratory spatial movement.
findings.reader_payoff: The closing pair becomes a felt movement from exposure and destructive refuge toward protected belonging, entry, and life-bearing shelter.
findings.containment: This exploratory cross-domain image carries the supplied womb facet into a spatial sequence without claiming that the focus adjective literally denotes a womb here. It remains anchored in the focus's mercy and protective covering, while the context supplies the opposed and favorable enclosures.
